title: FAK Run Operations
description: The default run-operations home: all open/live runs from the current descriptor inventory, completed-run review from durable root registrations, and separate historical usage economics. Stable UID fak-fleet-overview; source: `fak fleet metrics --serve` (scrape job fak_fleet).

options.content:
**Operate current runs, then review completed ones.** The open/live table is a projection of current session inventory. The completed table is a separate projection of durable root-run registrations, so an exited process remains reviewable without being counted as live. Click either table to open the same run drill-down.

Source: **`fak fleet metrics --serve --addr 127.0.0.1:9098`** (scrape job `fak_fleet`). If every panel reads *No data*, the exporter is not running — start it, or check `up{job="fak_fleet"}`.

**Sources stay separate.** `fak_fleet_session_*` / `fak_fleet_sessions*` are **LIVE**, read from the durable session registry by an oracle (PCB state, heartbeat freshness, resume's idle-vs-TTL posture) — the same fold `fak session ls --durable` prints. `fak_fleet_run_*` are **DURABLE RUN HISTORY**, read from root session registrations (the default `--registration-ledger`). `fak_fleet_usage_*` are **HISTORICAL USAGE**, folded from the append-only gateway-usage ledger, and their token/cache numbers are OBSERVED (provider-relayed) except the `kv_prefix_*` pair, which fak authored itself.

panels.title: Fleet source ready
panels.description: 1 when Prometheus can scrape the exporter. Start or restart with `tools/grafana/up.sh`; for a standalone source run `fak fleet metrics --serve --addr 127.0.0.1:9098`.

panels.title: Live inventory readable
panels.description: 0 means the live descriptor registry could not be read. It does not mean there are zero open runs.

panels.title: Run history readable
panels.description: 0 means the durable registration ledger could not be read. It does not mean no runs have completed.

panels.title: Fold freshness
panels.description: Age of the exporter's last fold; it should stay near the Prometheus scrape interval.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Sessions in the durable inventory — the same population `fak session ls --durable` prints.

panels.title: Live
panels.description: Running-family sessions whose durable heartbeat is fresh: alive AND progressing.

panels.title: Stalled
panels.description: Sessions that CLAIM a running state but whose heartbeat has not advanced within the stale window — claiming work, not progressing. This is the number worth alerting on.

panels.title: Idle
panels.description: Paused / stopped sessions. Idle is a resting state, not a fault.

panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: Distinct hosts carrying at least one session.

panels.title: Warm cache posture
panels.description: Sessions projected WARM by resume's idle-vs-TTL rule. A projection, never a witnessed provider-cache hit.

panels.title: Registered runs
panels.description: Root runs retained in durable lifecycle history. This count includes open and terminal registrations and is NOT liveness.

panels.title: Per-session rows dropped
panels.description: Sessions the --max-sessions cardinality bound kept OUT of the table below. Non-zero means the table is INCOMPLETE.

panels.title: All open / live runs — click one to drill down
Open / live runs (LIVE inventory)
panels.description: One row per non-terminal session in the LIVE descriptor inventory. `state` is the EFFECTIVE status: a RUNNING session with a lapsed heartbeat reads STALLED here, exactly as it does in the CLI headline. This table never reconstructs liveness from historical registration state.

panels.title: Completed registrations
panels.description: Root runs whose latest durable lifecycle state is completed.

panels.title: Failed / cancelled / lost
panels.description: Terminal root registrations that did not complete normally.

panels.title: Registration source ready
panels.description: Readiness of the durable run-history source.

panels.title: Completed runs (DURABLE registration history)
panels.description: One row per terminal root registration, retained after the live process exits. Creation, start, terminal time, duration, terminal reason, and witness reference support historical review; provenance remains `source=durable_registration`. Click its session id to review the run.

panels.title: Sessions by state over time
panels.description: Prometheus samples of the LIVE inventory over the selected time range. This is not durable completed-run history; use the registration table above.

panels.title: Liveness & cache posture over time
panels.description: Stalled climbing while live falls is the fleet wedging.

panels.title: Session age
panels.description: Seconds since each session was created. A very old session that is also STALLED is the classic reap candidate.

panels.title: Sessions per host
panels.description: Where the fleet is running. `unknown` is a session whose descriptor carries no host stamp, not a missing machine.

panels.title: Sessions folded
panels.description: Sessions in the ledger fold. A carryforward row (written by a ledger cut) expands to the row count it stands for, so a cut never silently shrinks this number.

panels.title: Turns
panels.description: OBSERVED served turns across the folded corpus.

panels.title: Cache read ratio
panels.description: cache_read / (input + cache_read + cache_creation). The denominator includes tokens paid to CREATE cache entries, so a session that only wrote cache is not credited with a hit.

panels.title: Cache read tokens
panels.description: OBSERVED prompt tokens the provider served from its cache.

panels.title: Cache creation tokens
panels.description: OBSERVED prompt tokens written INTO the provider's cache — a cost, not a saving.

panels.title: Input tokens
panels.description: OBSERVED uncached prompt tokens.

panels.title: Output tokens
panels.description: OBSERVED completion tokens.

panels.title: Drill-down coverage
panels.description: THE HONESTY GAUGE for the per-session panels below. The ledger's session_id is optional: a row written without one counts in every fleet total but can never appear in a per-session panel. Low coverage means the per-session cost view speaks for only a slice of the fleet. `fak serve` rows are deliberately unidentified — one serve process hosts a whole session table, so no single id would be true for its exit row.

panels.title: Token economy by session type
panels.description: The guard path (one process, one agent session) and the serve path (one process, many sessions) have different economics — never read them as one.

panels.title: Cache read ratio by session type
panels.description: A session type whose ratio is ABSENT folded no prompt tokens — unmeasured, not 0%.

panels.title: Top sessions by output tokens
panels.description: The fleet's biggest spenders, by name. Only sessions whose ledger rows carry a session_id can appear — see the drill-down coverage tile.

panels.title: Lowest cache read ratio by session
panels.description: Where cache reuse is worst. A session that folded no prompt tokens is ABSENT rather than ranked at 0% — unmeasured must not outrank genuinely bad.

panels.title: Kernel verdicts across the fleet
panels.description: The fleet-wide verdict mix, folded from the durable ledger. The per-session adjudication counts live on the drill-down dashboard.

panels.title: Ledger rows folded
panels.description: Rows the exporter folded after deduping by row key.

panels.title: Duplicate rows dropped
panels.description: Rows dropped as byte-identical duplicates of an already-folded row key (a retried flush). Ledger health, not fleet activity.

panels.title: Ledger last write
panels.description: Age of the newest ledger row. A value that keeps climbing means sessions stopped WRITING, which is not the same as the fleet going quiet.

panels.title: Fold freshness
panels.description: Age of the exporter's own fold. It re-folds on every scrape, so this should stay near the scrape interval.
